chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Riyab, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And whatever strike you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned; but He pardons much."
Tell me, what befell 'Ali and his Family, is it because of what their hands earned, while they are his Family, pure and infallible?

He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to repent to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and seek His forgiveness one hundred times every day and night, without any sin. Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, singles out His friends with afflictions to reward them for them without any sin.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Why do the Imams and Ahl al-Bayt suffer if they are sinless?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the afflictions suffered by the Ahl al-Bayt, such as the martyrdom of Imam Ali, are not punitive consequences of sin but rather divine trials designed to elevate their spiritual rank. This aligns with the broader Shia theological understanding that the Imams, though infallible, are subject to suffering as a means of accumulating extra reward (ajr) and demonstrating patience (sabr) to the faithful.

en.basel-kadem: 14.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Muhammed bin Hussain ibn Abi’l-Khattab, from Muhammed bin Isma’eel bin Bazee’, from Muhammed bin Ya’qoub bin Shu’aib, from his father, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

Indeed, people are narrating that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, did not fast the Month of Ramadan for twenty-nine (days) more than he fasted thirty (days). He said: They have lied. The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, did not fast but completely. Obligatory acts cannot be (performed whilst) lacking. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, created a year as having three hundred and sixty days, and He created the Heavens and the earth in six days, and so, He constrained it from three hundred and sixty. Hence, a year is (consisting of) three hundred and fifty-four days, and the Month of Ramadan is (consisting of) thirty days, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and that you may complete the period» [2:185]. That which is complete is (a) full (period). Shawwal is (consisting of) twenty-nine days, and Dhu’l-Qa’da is (consisting of) thirty days, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And We made an appointment with Musa for thirty nights» [7:142]. Hence, a month is like this. Furthermore, on this basis, a month is complete, and another month is lacking. The Month of Ramadan does never lack, and Sha’ban is never complete,
